'''Sidney "Sid" Morris''' (born 1947) is an Emeritus Professor at [[Federation University Australia]] who worked in the fields of mathematics and information technology. Before his retirement in 2010, he was a professor at several universities and received the 1987 [[Lester R. Ford]] award from the [[Mathematical Association of America]]. Morris is a fellow and former vice-president of the [[Australian Mathematical Society]] (AMS).

==Education==
Morris earned a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in 1969 from the [[University of Queensland]], Australia and one year later completed a Ph.D. at [[Flinders University]]. His dissertation, completed under the supervision of [[Igor Kluvanek]], defined the concept of "variety" among [[topological groups]] and proved a result similar to the [[Stone–Čech compactification]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Morris |first1=Sidney A. |title=Varieties of Topological Groups |journal=Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society |date=1969 |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=145–160 |doi=10.1017/S0004972700041393 |url=https://sidneymorris.net/Morris1.pdf}}</ref>

==Career==
During his first senior position at [[La Trobe University]], Morris began as an editor for the ''Bulletin of the [[Australian Mathematical Society]]''. He then became [[editor-in-chief]] of the ''Australian Mathematical Society Lecture Series'', a series published by [[Cambridge University Press]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Jones |first1=Arthur |last2=Gray |first2=Alistair |last3=Hutton |first3=Robert |title=Manifolds and mechanics |date=July 1987 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=9780521336505 |pages=i-iv |url=https://www.cambridge.org/au/universitypress/subjects/mathematics/differential-and-integral-equations-dynamical-systems-and-co/manifolds-and-mechanics?format=PB&isbn=9780521336505}}</ref>

In 1987, Morris received the [[Lester R. Ford]] award from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for the article ''Numerical Geometry – Numbers for Shapes''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cleary |first1=Joan |last2=Morris |first2=Sidney |last3=Yost |first3=David |title=Numerical geometry – numbers for shapes |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |date=1986 |volume=93 |issue=4 |pages=139–144 |doi=10.1080/00029890.1986.11971802 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Paul R. Halmos – Lester R. Ford Awards – Mathematical Association of America |url=https://maa.org/paul-r-halmos-lester-r-ford-awards/ |website=Mathematical Association of America |access-date=22 July 2025 |archive-date=22 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250622050110/https://maa.org/paul-r-halmos-lester-r-ford-awards/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Morris published his first book ''The Structure of Compact Groups'' in 1998 with {{ill|Karl Heinrich Hofmann|de}}.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Netuka |first1=Ivan |last2=Souèek |first2=Vladimír |date=June 1999 |title=Recent books |url=https://ems.press/content/serial-issue-files/13602 |journal=European Mathematical Society Newsletter |volume=32 |pages=33}}</ref> He, along with Arthur Jones and Kenneth R. Pearson, published ''Abstract Algebra and Famous Impossibilities'' in 2022 as part of [[Springer Publishing|Springer]]'s [[Undergraduate Texts in Mathematics]] series.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Morris |first1=Sidney A. |last2=Jones |first2=Arthur |last3=Pearson |first3=Kenneth R. |title=Abstract Algebra and Famous Impossibilities: Squaring the Circle, Doubling the Cube, Trisecting an Angle, and Solving Quintic Equations |date=2022 |publisher=Springer |location=Cham, Switzerland |isbn=978-3-031-05697-0 |edition=Second |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-05698-7 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-05698-7}}</ref>

Although he is retired, Morris remains an editor for the AMS's ''Gazette'' and [[MDPI]]'s ''Internation Journal of Topology''.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Frontmatter |journal=Gazette |date=2025 |volume=52 |issue=2 |page=i |url=https://austms.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/522Web-3.pdf |publisher=Australian Mathematical Society}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://www.mdpi.com/journal/ijt/editors |website=mdpi.com |access-date=22 July 2025}}</ref> He continues to maintain his [[online book]] ''Topology Without Tears'', which was initially published in 1985.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Morris |first1=Sidney A. |title=Topology Without Tears |url=https://www.topologywithouttears.net/topbook.pdf |access-date=22 July 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sidney Morris received his [[rabbinical ordination]] in 2016 at the age of 68.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Roth |first1=Phoebe |title=It's never too late |url=https://www.australianjewishnews.com/its-never-too-late/ |website=www.australianjewishnews.com}}</ref> He has been married to his wife, Elizabeth, for over fifty years.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Morris |first1=Sid |title=Biography |url=https://www.sidneymorris.net/bio.htm |access-date=22 July 2025 |archive-date=14 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250714164544/https://sidneymorris.net/bio.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>
